topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture series on cancer causes, and states the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Processes versus Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the fundamental causes of cancer by examining how intrinsic mutational processes and environmental exposures contribute to malignancy.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignancy, highlighting the interplay between viral infection and environmental co-factors in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce mutagenic DNA damage, focusing on their metabolic activation into reactive derivatives.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor promotion, microenvironmental inflammation, and host developmental context permit malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the methodologies used by researchers to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of environmental agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure in terms of personal risk-benefit choices and summarizing the main takeaways.
